office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: First-term Republican Rep. David Stuebe, also mayor of Washougal, won the seat by under 900 votes in 2024 and faces Democrat Diana H. Perez, a Vancouver city councilor and retired Forest Service manager. Stuebe campaigns on no new taxes and spending limits; Perez pairs state housing investment with permitting reform and backs the clean-energy transition with cost caveats.

candidates.summary: Vancouver city councilor since 2022 and former state parks and housing finance commissioner, with 30-plus years in Forest Service natural-resource management, running on housing costs, infrastructure, schools and public safety.
highlights: Would increase state investment in affordable housing while cutting permitting delays and regulatory barriers [S3]
Cast the only council vote against Vancouver's 0.1% public-safety sales tax, citing the cumulative tax burden [S8]
Says climate change is real and the energy transition must not jeopardize grid reliability or raise utility costs [S3]
Recommended by The Columbian's editorial board [S6]

spending.basis: Pledges 'living within our budgetary means' and fiscal responsibility alongside more state investment in housing, schools and infrastructure.

housing.basis: Combines more state investment in affordable housing and homelessness prevention with reducing permitting delays and regulatory barriers.

safety.basis: Wants adequate law-enforcement staffing alongside prevention, behavioral health and victim support: 'both immediate response and long-term prevention.'

climate.basis: Calls the clean-energy transition essential but says it must not jeopardize grid reliability or raise utility costs.

experience.basis: No legislative tenure, but a sitting city councilor since 2022 and former state commissioner, running against a first-term legislator.

candidates.summary: First-term Republican incumbent, mayor of Washougal and retired Marine Corps colonel, running on lowering costs, public safety and holding state government accountable.
highlights: Voted against ESSB 6346 and the 2025 revenue bills; says "I voted no on a state income tax" [S3][S5][S6][S7][S1]
Offered an amendment to cut the state sales tax from 6.5% to 5%; it failed 43-52 [S4]
Calls for no new taxes, a two-thirds vote to raise them and tying budget growth to inflation and population [S15]
His bill HB 2531, on ambulance Medicaid funding, was signed in 2026 [S16]

taxes.basis: Voted no on ESSB 6346 and three 2025 revenue bills, sponsored a sales-tax cut amendment and calls for no new taxes and a two-thirds vote to raise them.

spending.basis: Says the state has 'a spending problem,' wants budget growth tied to inflation and population, programs without returns cut, and voted against the 2025-27 budget.

housing.basis: Voted against limits on rent and fee increases (EHB 1217) and faults the majority for no regulatory relief to speed housing construction.

safety.basis: Counts blocking shorter sentences for serious crimes and limits on local camping-law enforcement as wins; pamphlet commits to strengthening public safety.

climate.basis: Voted against the clean fuels program bill (2SHB 1409) and counts blocking a data-center energy tax and a wildfire utility surcharge as wins.

healthcare.basis: Wants Medicaid access and 2025 Medicaid funding restored and more support for rural hospitals within the current system; sponsored an ambulance Medicaid bill.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296, which changed the parental rights enacted by Initiative 2081; no position on I-1 found.

experience.basis: First-term legislator and sitting Washougal mayor, running against a city councilor without legislative tenure.
